Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. Ireland players are seen out in a huddle near the ropes. Jos Buttler and Alex Hales walk in with their blades for England. Josh Little comes to bowl. Here we go.
... The Run Chase ...
Right then, England will be hoping for a clinical chasing effort this time round, while Andy Balbirnie will be hoping for some early inroads from his new ball bowlers. Chase coming up in a bit…

Mark Wood is in for a chat now. He says that they did not bowl well. Shares that the he was worried about landing due to wet and greasy conditions. Reckons that they bowled too many full deliveries and did not have the intensity at the start. Adds that 157 is a good score to chase. Credits Liam Livingstone for his brilliant spell. Feels that he bowled with some good speed but could have been better.

England, unfortunately, failed to take full advantage of the new ball in overcast conditions. They resorted to short-pitched bowling and paid the price. After dismissing Tucker in the 13th over, England clawed their way back into the game with some quick wickets. Liam Livingstone and Mark Wood combined to account for six Irish wickets bagging three each whilst Sam Curran took two.

So, Ireland end up with 157 on the board. Ireland will be disappointed that they let it slip from a strong position with the bat. Jos Buttler will be happy with the way the bowlers brought them back into the game. Having been sent into bat first, Ireland's batters did a great job of not losing more than one wicket in the powerplay. The pair of Andrew Balbirnie and Lorcan Tucker kept the scoreboard ticking in testing conditions against the moving new ball. Once the 82-run stand was broken, Ireland lost their way a bit and struggled for the rest of the innings and lost wickets in a trot.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Stokes gets the last wicket and Ireland have been bowled out for 157! Stokes lands a good-length delivery, around off. Little tries to push it towards the off side. However, the ball catches the thin outside edge of his blade and Buttler takes an easy catch behind the stumps. Brilliant comeback by England this!
Commentary.Howout: c Jos Buttler b Ben Stokes

Commentary.Commentary: A fullish delivery, outside off. Delany slices it to deep point for a single.
Josh Little is the last batter. Ben Stokes to bowl the final over.

OUT! BOWLED! Curran hits his target again and Hand has to walk back to the hut now. Curran comes 'round the wicket again and bowls a length delivery angling into the stumps. Hand makes room and tries to play the inside-out shot. He misses and the ball knocks over the stumps.

Oh, dear...that it poor from Wood! Back of a length and around off. Delany guides it to short third man where Wood fails to get down in time and the batters take three as the ball rolls towards the third man fence before the fielder cuts it off.
Goes 'round the wicket and bowls a shortish delivery angling into off. Delany tries to pull it but misses.
A slower length ball on middle. Hand makes room and dabs it towards the off side for a quick single.
Fionn Hand is the next batter.

OUT! BOWLED! Another one bites the dust! Sam Curran nails a yorker this time. It is on middle and Barry McCarthy makes room to hit it towards the off side. He misses and the ball shatters the stumps. Eight down now Ireland and the question is, can they get to 165-run mark from here?
A slower length delivery on the pads. Barry McCarthy clips it to deep mid-wicket and comes back for the second run. Good running.
Loopy delivery, outside off. Barry McCarthy drives it to deep point for a single. 150 up for Ireland!
Barry McCarthy walks in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Liam Livingstone gets his third wicket! He tosses this up nicely, on middle. Adair tries to clear the longer boundary towards the leg side and goes for the slog-sweep. However, he fails to get enough power behind his shot and ends up hitting it to Sam Curran at deep mid-wicket who takes an easy catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Sam Curran b Liam Livingstone

Commentary.Commentary: Tad short and angling into middle and leg again. Adair skips down the track and works it to deep mid-wicket for a couple.
A quicker one and flatter as well, on middle. Delany knocks it down towards mid on for a single.
Floated up on middle. Adair drives it to long on for a single.
Tossed up, outside off. Delany drives it to deep point for a single.
There is a concussion protocol being followed by the Ireland physio as Gareth Delany gets a hit on his helmet. The test is complete and we are good to go.

Oh, Wood hits another batter on the helmet! A bouncer angling into middle. Delany tries to duck under it but the ball is too quick and does not bounce much as it hits his helmet. A leg bye is taken though as the ball deflects towards fine leg.
FOUR! Lovely shot! Wood delivers another full delivery, outside off. Delany opens the face of his blade and creams it through the backward point region for a boundary.

Just short! A fullish delivery, outside off. Adair slices it uppishly towards third man and the fielder in the deep runs forward and dives to take it. However, the ball falls just ahead of him. Single taken.
Mark Adair is the next batter.

OUT! CAUGHT! Mark Wood strikes again! A sharp catch from Buttler behind the stumps as well and Irish are losing their way here. Wood delivers a short delivery, around leg. Campher tries to pull it but does not get much bat on it and just enough to hit it left of Buttler. The English skipper dives and takes a brilliant catch and Ireland are six down now.
Commentary.Howout: c Jos Buttler b Mark Wood

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Handy boundary for Ireland, this will ease some pressue. Pacy delivery at 148 kph. Lands on a length, on off. Campher gets across to his right and uses the pace of the ball to scoop it over short fine leg for a boundary.
Back of a length, on leg. Delany works it to fine leg for a single.
A flatter one on middle. Gareth Delany clips it to the leg side and gets off the mark with a single.
No hat-trick! Liam fires this on middle. Gareth Delany manages to get his bat down in time.
Gareth Delany is the new batter. Liam Livingstone is on a hat-trick. Can he take it?

OUT! BOWLED! Two in two for Liam Livingstone and he is absolutely pumped up! Another tossed up delivery on middle. George Dockrell facing his first delivery, makes some room and tries to drive it. However, he misses it completely and the ball goes onto knock the stumps. England are making a strong comeback here! Liam Livingstone is on a hat-trick!
George Dockrell walks in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Andy Balbirnie holes out in the deep! Truly against the run of play this but England will take it. Brilliant knock from Andy Balbirnie comes to an end. This is slower through the air again, on off. Andy Balbirnie sweeps and sweeps quite well but it goes aerially and straight to Alex Hales at fine leg. He takes an easy catch and England continue to take wickets after the 10-over mark!
Commentary.Howout: c Alex Hales b Liam Livingstone

Commentary.Commentary: Shortish length, on off. Campher makes room and cuts it to deep point for a single.
FOUR! Boundaries continue to flow here! This is tossed up on middle. Campher gets a bit across to his right and scoops it past short fine leg for a boundary. Excellent batsmanship!
Back of a length and around off. Andy Balbirnie makes room and tries to swing it across the line but misses.
Serves it fuller this time angling into the pads. Andy Balbirnie clips it to deep backward square leg for a couple.
Back of a length and angling across the batter, around off. Andy Balbirnie tries to cut it but misses.
SIX! Wow! The Irish skipper is turning it on! A shortish delivery on off. Andy Balbirnie stays deep in his crease and pulls it fimly and deep into the stands over the square leg fence.
On a length and around off. Andy Balbirnie makes room and slaps it to sweeper cover for a couple.
Campher makes room and Curran follows him. This is full and on the pads. Campher tries to clip it but misses as the ball hits his pads. A leg bye is taken.
Sam Curran is back on.
Flighted outside off, Andy Balbirnie slaps this one wide of long off for a couple of runs more.
Wrong-un on middle, Curtis Campher doesn't read it and gets an inside edge as he tried to cut. The batters take a single as the ball rolls on the off side.
Full on off, Andy Balbirnie gets forward and clips it to mid wicket for a single to bring up a well-composed fifty. His 8th fifty in the T20I's!
Tossed up outside off, Curtis Campher shuffles across and slog sweeps it to deep square leg for a single.
Flighted on off, Andy Balbirnie taps it on the off and gets a single.
Floated outside off, Curtis Campher knocks it to long off for a single.
A dot to end the over. Bowls it on a length and on middle, Andy Balbirnie defends it to backward point.
Slightly shorter and outside off, Curtis Campher guides it to backward point for one.
Curtis Campher has been hit on his helmet! We will have a mandatory concussion test now. He looks fine to continue now and we are ready to resume.
Shorter one on middle, Curtis Campher looks to pull it but the ball hits his helmet and bounces off the deck.
FOUR! Fine shot. Fuller and outside off, Curtis Campher slices it over backward point for a boundary. Ireland needs to regroup now.
Wide! Bowls it outside leg, Curtis Campher lets it go.
Curtis Campher is the next man in.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! This one lands on a length and just outside off, Harry Tector looks to loft it but gets a thin outside edge. The ball goes safely into the gloves of Jos Buttler and Ireland lose two wickets in quick succession. Credit should be given to Buttler as well for bringing in Wood straightaway after the wicket.
Commentary.Howout: c Jos Buttler b Mark Wood

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and outside off, Harry Tector looks to defend it but misses.
Harry Tector walks out to the middle as Mark Wood is back into the attack as well. Buttler sensing an opportunity here!

OUT! UNLUCKY DISMISSAL! Floated on off, Andy Balbirnie hits it straight back towards the bowler. Rashid gets a hand on it on its way to the stumps. Lorcan Tucker is out of his crease as the ball hits the stumps. A much-needed wicket for England. Lorcan Tucker is disappointed and rightly so, he was looking pretty confident out there in the middle.
Tossed up outside off, Lorcan Tucker shimmies down the track to slog it down the ground. Gets an inside edge that rolls towards square leg.
Flatter at the pads, Andy Balbirnie nudges it to deep mid wicket for a single.
Flighted on middle, Lorcan Tucker gets on his knee and sweeps it to square leg for a run.
Flighted on off, Andy Balbirnie gets forward and works it to long on for a single.
Full and on middle, Andy Balbirnie shuffles and drills it through extra covers for a couple.
Fuller and on off, Andy Balbirnie sweeps it to square leg for one.
Play and a miss. This one lands on leg, Andy Balbirnie looks to sweep it but misses as he ball hits his thigh pad. Dot.
Another single as this is played towards mid on.
Fuller one on off, Andy Balbirnie eases it to covers for one more.
This one lands down leg, Lorcan Tucker flicks it to mid-wicket for one again.
Slightly shorter and outside off, Andy Balbirnie taps it to point for one.

Drinks break. This has been a fantastic start for the Irish. They have gone about their business with a fearless attitude despite losing Paul Stirling early and now have a good platform to set a huge total here. English bowlers, on the other hand, have been pretty ordinary and need to tighten up, if they want to make their way back into this game. An interesting phase of the game coming up as Liam Livingstone is introduced into the attack.
Back of a length on middle, Andy Balbirnie drops it on the off side and takes a single. This 18-run over is now the most expensive over of the innings.
SIX! Short and at the batter, Andy Balbirnie picks it up from his hip and deposits this one over fine leg for a maximum. This is turning out to be a very expensive over by Chris Woakes.

FOUR! Slower and into the wicket, Andy Balbirnie creates the pace by advancing down the track and smashes this one over deep mid-wicket for the second boundary of the over. The fielder in the deep was standing a few yards in from the boundary.
Slower and at the body, Lorcan Tucker works it to fine leg for a single.
Short on off, Andy Balbirnie knocks it off the back foot to mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Short down the leg side, Andy Balbirnie uses the pace and works it behind square leg for a boundary. The fielder in the deep ran to his right but could not prevent the boundary.
WIDE! Woakes sprays it down the legside. Good take by Buttler diving to his left as Andy Balbirnie dances down the track while making room to heave it away.
Fuller length and around off. Andy Balbirnie strides forward and pushes it down to long on for one.
Tossed up, outside off. Andy Balbirnie drives it to extra covers for a brace.
Play and a miss. This one lands outside off, Andy Balbirnie looks to play at it but misses.
Fuller length outside the off. Tucker comes down the track and heaves it to mid-wicket for one. 50 partnership up between Lorcan Tucker and Andy Balbirnie.
Goes fuller again, on off. Lorcan Tucker plays a reverse sweep to backward point for one.
Fuller one and on off, Andy Balbirnie steers it to long off for one.
Good length on off, Andy Balbirnie taps it on the off side and rushes for a quick single.
Bumper outside off, Lorcan Tucker shuffles across and pulls it towards deep mid wicket for a single.
Full outside off, Andy Balbirnie jams it towards deep point for a single.
Back of a length on leg, Tucker helps it towards fine leg for a single.
Back of a length and around off. Tucker opens the bat face and dabs it down to backward point.
Good-length delivery outside off, Andy Balbirnie advances and pokes it at it but misses.
Ben Stokes is back on. Can he break this partnership?
Bowls it outside off, Andy Balbirnie guides it straight towards the fielder at point.
Fuller one again, Lorcan Tucker nudges it to mid-wicket for one.
Fuller and down leg, Lorcan Tucker looks to sweep it but misses and gets his pads. A stifled appeal turned down.
Tossed up with a hint of turn, Lorcan Tucker defends it back towards the bowler.
On off, fuller in length. Andy Balbirnie guides it to short third man for one.
FOUR! Fine shot. A low full toss wide outside off, Andy Balbirnie slices it over point for a boundary!

SIX! STRAIGHT HIT! Lorcan Tucker advances down the track and converts a good delivery into a full one. Lofts this one with a straight bat towards long on for his first six of the game. Ireland are 59 for one after the Powerplay!
Banged in short by Curran, Tucker fails to get bat on it as he looked to ramp it over the keeper.
Short and at the body, Lorcan Tucker works it gently towards square leg and collects a brace.
Back of a length on middle, Tucker gets beaten as he tried to open the bat face and play it fine.
FOUR! DISPATCHED! Low full toss on off, Tucker moves away and drills it past Ben Stokes at mid off. Stokes went to his left first and then dived to his right but failed to stop it.
Short down the leg side, Lorcan Tucker tucks this one behind square for a couple of runs.
Sam Curran is brought into the attack now.
Bowls it outside off, Andy Balbirnie guides it to third man for a brace. 8 runs off the over.
Shorter and on leg, Lorcan Tucker pulls it to short fine leg for one.
Slightly shorter and down leg, Andy Balbirnie looks to flick it but gets his thigh. The ball rolls towards the left of the keeper. They cross for a leg bye.
Shorter one this time, Andy Balbirnie ducks underneath it.
FOUR! On a length and on off, Andy Balbirnie shuffles across and smashes it over point for a boundary!
Andy Balbirnie seems to be in some pain here. He has hurt his right hand's index finger and is getting some treatment from the physio. Looks fine now and we are ready to resume.
Slightly shorter and on off, Andy Balbirnie hands back and defends it out.
FOUR! Poor delivery by Woakes. Bowls it short without much pace, Lorcan Tucker makes room and smashes this one past the ring on the off side for the second boundary of the over.
Short of a length on middle, Tucker shimmies down the track to work it on the off side and gets beaten.
Slower and back of a length outside off, Andy Balbirnie taps it to backward point and takes a single.
Full on leg, Lorcan Tucker flicks this one to deep square leg for a run. The batters wanted a second but decided against it.
FOUR! Smart batting by Tucker. Good length delivery outside off, Tucker knows the fielder behind square is inside the circle. He shuffles across and scoops it over short fine leg for a boundary.
Back of a length on leg, Andy Balbirnie clips it off the back foot to square leg for a single.
Back of a length and outside off, Lorcan Tucker looks to play at it but misses.

FOUR WIDES! This one lands shorter and on leg, Andy Balbirnie ducks it. Buttler dives to his left and half-stops it. While the batters take a run off it, Buttler misses the shy at the bowler's end and allows the batters to run through for a couple more. Wide called as well.
Slightly shorter angling it away from the batter, Andy Balbirnie gets beaten off the outside edge.
Shorter again, on off. Lorcan Tucker fends it towards the off side for one.
Lorcan Tucker walks out at number 3!

OUT! CAUGHT! Shorter again, outside off. Paul Stirling looks to slap it but miscues it to third man. The ball goes in the air. Sam Curran settles under it and pouches it comfortably with both hands. England have an early breakthrough in the game. Paul Stirling makes his way back into the hut.
Commentary.Howout: c Sam Curran b Mark Wood

Commentary.Commentary: Play and a miss. This one lands outside off, Paul Stirling looks to play at it but misses.

SIX! Dropped! Shorter one on off, Paul Stirling looks to pull it but gets a top edge. The ball goes towards third man. The fielder at the third man takes a catch but he was in contact with the ropes. A good try from the fielder but its a maximum.
Mark Wood is into the attack now.

FOUR! Good length swinging away from the batter. Balbirnie makes room to free his arms and slices this one over covers for his first boundary. The ball went to the boundary even after Balbirnie got it off the bottom part of the bat.
Back of a length on middle, Balbirnie gets rapped on the thigh as he went for the flick.
Full and shaping away on off, Andy Balbirnie drives it uppishly towards point.
We are back! No overs have been lost yet and the the English players and Irish openers are back on the field as well. Chris Woakes to resume his over. Here we go...
Update - 10.11 am IST (4.41 am GMT) - The rain has eased out, and the covers are off. Let's hope we have a start soon. Fingers crossed.

Update - 9.56 am IST (4.26 am GMT) - The rain is back! It is heavier this time and players are running off the field as covers come on. This could be a longer delay and there is high chance now that we lose some overs if the rain continues to put on a show here.
Full outside off, Paul Stirling moves away and carves this one in the air through the offside. The batters come back for three.
Short of a length outside off, Paul Stirling tries to defend it off the backfoot and gets beaten.
WIDE! Full and going away, Stirling makes room to slice it but fails to make any contact. The umpire calls it a wide. Woakes is getting some good shape with this new ball.
FOUR! Full and swinging away from the batter, Stirling opens the bat face and guides it past backward point for his first boundary. Good timing and placement from Paul Stirling!
Chris Woakes to share the new ball with Ben Stokes!
On a length and on middle angling it into the batter, Andy Balbirnie awkwardly defends it away. A dot to end the over.
Bowls it outside off, a bit fuller too. Andy Balbirnie leaves it alone.
Good length angling it away, Andy Balbirnie defends it back towards Ben Stokes.
Goes outside off, Andy Balbirnie guides it to backward point for a brace.
Slightly shorter this time, Paul Stirling slices it away to backward point and gets off the mark. They cross.
Starts with a length ball on off, Paul Stirling defends it out solidly. A dot to start with.

The rain has cleared! The English players are on the field and the Irish openers, Andy Balbirnie and Paul Stirling are walking into the middle as well. Ben Stokes to start with the ball. Here we go...

Update - 9.43 am IST (4.13 am GMT) - Just when we were about to start, the rain is back again. It is that kind of day here in Melbourne, hopefully we will have better news soon. As of now, the start of the game is delayed further.
The anthems are done but we will have a slight delay here. The game will start at 9.45 am IST (4.15 am GMT).

Now then, the players are walking on the field for the national anthems. The pitch is still covered though and we are ready for the anthems now. We will have England's anthem first which will be followed by the Irish one.

There is always some spice when these two neighbours go head-to-head in any sports but for now we have to deal with rain, it is drizzling at the moment and covers have come on. It is not that hard though and players are standing near the fence. Also, the spectators are not using their umbrellas either, so we can expect to start soon.

Andy Balbirnie, the skipper of Ireland says that they would have chased as well with rain around but adds that they need to do their best now. Tells that they need to come out with aggression and a positive approach against the top-class bowlers. Tells that they have played a practice game here and they will try to make special memories just liked they did in Hobart. Says that they have happy memories of the 2011 World Cup and adds that they would like to replicate the same in MCG. Informs they have made one change with Fionn Hand coming in for Simi Singh.

Jos Buttler, the skipper of England says that they will bowl first and the weather has influenced his decision to bowl first. Shares that this a huge game for them. Adds that they have set high fielding standards considering the huge playing fields in Australia. Informs that they are going with the same team as the last game.
England (Unchanged Playing XI) - Jos Buttler (C) (WK), Alex Hales, Dawid Malan, Ben Stokes, Liam Livingstone, Harry Brook, Moeen Ali, Sam Curran, Chris Woakes, Adil Rashid, Mark Wood.

Ireland (Playing XI) - Paul Stirling, Andy Balbirnie (C), Lorcan Tucker (WK), Harry Tector, Curtis Campher, George Dockrell, Gareth Delany, Mark Adair, Fionn Hand (In place of Simi Singh), Barry McCarthy, Josh Little.
TOSS - The coin goes up and lands in favour of England. They have elected to BOWL first.

PITCH REPORT - Isa Guha is down for the Pitch Report. She says that this is a fresh pitch and adds that both teams would be looking to exploit comparatively short straight boundaries. Shane Watson joins her and says that the wicket looks nice if you are a fast bowler and there is a live green grass on the pitch. Adds that there is some moisture in the sureface and there will be some tennis-ball bounce. Mentions that the skipper that wins the toss would like to chase as that has been the way in MCG.

Andy Balbirnie shall be worried about the form of his bowlers heading into this big game. The side went down by 9 wickets against Sri Lanka in the last game, where most of their bowlers failed to apply pressure on the opponents. They would hope to put up a better show in this game. Ireland have always shown its giant-killing traits in the past, and it will be interesting to look at their approach in this game. Can they pull up a shocker? Stay tuned to find out. Toss and team news in a bit.

Jos Buttler's side has started the tournament on a positive note. They defeated Afghanistan by 5 wickets in their last game. The bowling attack made excellent use of the conditions to restrict the Afghans to a small total. Buttler though would look for an improved show from his batters as they showed signs of struggle in their small run chase in the last game. Expect them to come out all guns blazing in this game.

Hello and a warm welcome to match 8 of the Super 12 as England would be up against Ireland. It was a good start for England in the tournament, as the 2010 T20 World Cup Champions defeated Afghanistan in their first game of the tournament. The Irish side shall feel some heat in this game after their massive defeat against the Lankans. They were hammered to all parts of the ground in the last game. This will surely be another tough challenge against England, who have one of the strongest batting line-ups.
... MATCH DAY …
